/-!
# Primes and perfect squares

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landau%27s_problems#Near-square_primes)
-/


namespace PrimesAndPerfectSquares

/--
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p - 1$ is a perfect square? In other words: Are there infinitely many primes of the form $n^2 + 1$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_prime_sq_add_one :
    answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | Prime (n^2 + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end PrimesAndPerfectSquares

reformulations.difference: The source asks for infinitely many primes p with p − 1 a perfect square, equivalently p = n² + 1 for integer n. Lean instead asks whether infinitely many natural-number parameters n make n² + 1 prime.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, generic Prime is equivalent to Nat.Prime by Nat.prime_iff. The map n ↦ n² + 1 is injective on ℕ, and its image on the prime-producing parameters is exactly {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ IsSquare (p − 1)}. Allowing integer roots gives the same prime values, since squaring an integer or its natural absolute value gives the same result. Thus the parameter set is infinite exactly when the source's prime set is infinite. Both equivalences, also preserved under an arbitrary propositional answer slot, were proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without sorry.
